what_it_does: When engineers want to understand how fast a large language model (LLM) will run on a GPU before buying hardware or changing software, they use an analytical model — a mathematical formula that predicts performance without running the actual code. Existing models are inaccurate because they incorrectly estimate the speed of the GPU's dedicated matrix-multiplication units (the chip's fast math hardware), ignore delays from small on-chip instruction and constant caches, and oversimplify how the GPU manages parallel execution threads (called warps). AMALI fixes all three gaps: it models the math-unit pipeline fill and drain behavior accurately, adds micro-benchmark-measured models for the small caches, and uses per-warp instruction counts to reflect realistic scheduling. The result is validated against measurements on real A100 GPU hardware, giving engineers a trustworthy performance predictor for LLM inference workloads.
